title: Catching the Whole Picture

patient.name: Mdm Fatimah binte Osman
patient.presenting_complaint: Booked for fundus photography to document a pigmented lesion the doctor wants monitored

history.hpc: Mdm Fatimah was referred from clinic for colour fundus photography of the right eye to document a peripheral pigmented choroidal lesion, plus disc and macula images of both eyes for a baseline. She has no acute visual symptoms today. She is anxious about the bright flashes.
history.pmhx: Type 2 diabetes, hypertension. No known dye allergy. Not on any anticoagulant.
history.social_hx: Works long hours standing; needs to return to work same day.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Quiet anterior segments; pupils dilate adequately after tropicamide; anterior chambers deep (safe to dilate)
examination_findings.fundus: Right eye: flat, well-demarcated pigmented peripheral lesion; disc and macula normal. Left eye: normal disc and macula.

investigations.fundus_photography: After confirming safe-to-dilate and instilling mydriatic, well-focused colour fundus photographs obtained: disc-centred and macula-centred fields both eyes, plus a peripheral steered field capturing the right pigmented lesion for documentation. Images correctly labelled by patient and eye.
investigations.quality_control: Eyepiece/dioptre focused; alignment and working distance set to avoid arc/edge artefacts and lash shadows; flash intensity adjusted for media clarity; a repeat frame taken where the first showed a reflection artefact. No dye/angiography required for this documentation request.
investigations.safety_checks: Confirmed adequate mydriasis and deep anterior chamber before dilating; warned the patient about transient blur/light sensitivity afterwards.

diagnosis: Good-quality documentary colour fundus photographs of both eyes with a dedicated peripheral field capturing the right choroidal pigmented lesion for baseline monitoring. Images handed to the ophthalmologist for interpretation; the technician captures and documents but does not diagnose the lesion.

immediate: Confirm identity and the imaging request (which eye, which fields, colour vs angiography)
Check it is safe to dilate (anterior chamber depth) and instil the mydriatic, confirming adequate dilation
Focus the eyepiece/dioptre and align the camera to avoid arc, edge, and lash artefacts
Capture disc- and macula-centred fields of both eyes plus a steered peripheral field for the lesion
Review each frame for focus, illumination, and artefacts; repeat any inadequate frame
Label every image by patient identity and correct eye before saving
follow_up: Store and route the labelled images to the ophthalmologist for interpretation
Note that no angiography/dye was needed for this documentation request
Advise on post-dilation precautions before she returns to work
patient_education: Explain the camera photographs the back of the eye and the flashes are bright but harmless
Warn that dilation causes a few hours of blur and light sensitivity; advise sunglasses and no driving until it settles
Reassure that the pictures are for the doctor to review and monitor the lesion over time

key_points: Confirms the exact imaging request (eye, fields, colour photography vs angiography)
Checks dilation safety (anterior chamber depth) and any dye-allergy/anticoagulant relevance
Addresses the patient's anxiety about the flashes
Notes her need to return to work when advising on dilation
Focuses the eyepiece/dioptre and aligns to avoid arc/edge/lash artefacts
Captures the required fields including a steered peripheral field for the lesion
Reviews frames and repeats inadequate images; labels by patient and eye
Recognises the goal is documentation/baseline of the pigmented lesion, not diagnosis
Selects the correct fields for the request
Judges image quality (focus, illumination, artefacts) adequately
Stays within scope — captures and documents, leaves interpretation to the ophthalmologist
Stores and routes correctly labelled images to the ophthalmologist
Documents that no angiography/dye was required
